narrative.intro: Regents of the University of California obligated $1.2B in FY2026 to date across 3 awards, with an average award size of $410M. Obligations fell 5.9% year over year. The Department of Energy accounted for the largest share of buying activity with $1.2B in obligations. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences is the largest market by obligations at $1.2B, followed by Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools at $4M and Computer Facilities Management Services at $31.3K. Historical fiscal-year obligations show large swings: FY21 was $67.4M, FY22 was $6.7M, FY23 was $982M, FY24 was $1.4B, FY25 was $1.3B, and FY26 is $1.2B to date. Current-year totals are partial because figures represent fiscal year to date and some award-value tables report total contract values rather than obligations. This profile shows heavy concentration in a single agency and a single NAICS market for the current fiscal year to date.

sections.heading: How concentrated are Regents of the University of California's federal obligations?
sections.body: Regents of the University of California's FY2026 to date obligations are highly concentrated. The Department of Energy obligated $1.2B, which matches the total obligations for the vendor in FY2026 to date. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences accounted for $1.2B of obligations. Secondary agency and market activity is minimal, with the Department of Commerce at $31.3K and Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools at $4M.

sections.heading: How have obligations for Regents of the University of California changed over time?
sections.body: Regents of the University of California's obligations rose and fell sharply across recent fiscal years. Fiscal-year obligations were $67.4M in FY21, $6.7M in FY22, $982M in FY23, $1.4B in FY24, $1.3B in FY25, and $1.2B in FY26 to date. Obligations fell 5.9% year over year into FY2026 to date. The current-year totals are partial and reported fiscal year to date.
